title: Free nightly offsets erase the exact GJ 3543 alias separation for fixed four-hour pairs on sidereal nights
abstract: We test a GJ 3543 observing plan against unknown nightly velocity offsets. For exact daily alias frequencies, fixed pair spacing, and integer sidereal nights, the two sine models span the same space after pair subtraction. Free nightly offsets thus remove all alias separation. A 40-visit test with a stable 2.73 m/s signal recovers about 97 percent correct choices with independent noise, but gives random ties with free offsets. Three variable-spacing designs break exact equality but give only 50 to 62 percent correct choices at the tested errors. Public HARPS-RVBank version 02 contains 96 accepted visits on separate dates and gives no within-night contrast under the tested offset model. These are conditional design results. We do not measure the true offset variance, confirm a planet, or identify an instrumental cause. Independent instrument confirmation is absent. Code, frozen input, source hashes, proof, simulations, checks, and offline steps are included.

display.caption: Fixed-period choices with known Gaussian nightly covariance and with free offsets. Error bars show 1.96 Monte Carlo standard errors. All results assume a stable 2.73 m/s sinusoid and 40 visits.

citations.reason: We test the nightly-offset limit of its fixed-pair schedule. We reuse its target periods and design assumptions, but no source code.
